question: An 80-year-old man presents with intensely itchy, tense dome-shaped bullae on an erythematous base over the trunk and limbs. He has no oral lesions. Nikolsky's sign is negative. Which statement about his likely diagnosis is correct?

answers.text: Bullous pemphigoid — sub-epidermal split, linear basement-membrane IgG/C3 on DIF, anti-BP180/BP230 antibodies

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Tense bullae in an elderly patient, with the mouth spared, pruritus, and a negative Nikolsky's sign are classic for bullous pemphigoid — a sub-epidermal disease with linear IgG/C3 along the basement membrane on DIF and anti-BP180/BP230 antibodies.

answers.text: Pemphigus vulgaris — intra-epidermal split, intercellular fish-net IgG on DIF, anti-desmoglein 3 antibodies

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pemphigus vulgaris produces flaccid (not tense) bullae, typically in middle-aged adults, with prominent oral involvement and a positive Nikolsky's sign. This elderly patient with tense bullae, no mouth lesions, and a negative Nikolsky sign has bullous pemphigoid.

answers.text: Bullous pemphigoid — with expected acantholytic cells on Tzanck smear and a positive Nikolsky's sign

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Acantholytic cells on Tzanck smear and a positive Nikolsky's sign are features of pemphigus vulgaris, not bullous pemphigoid. In BP the epidermis stays intact (negative Nikolsky) and the Tzanck smear is unremarkable.

answers.text: Pemphigus vulgaris — because the patient is elderly and the mouth is spared

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Elderly age and mucosal sparing actually favour bullous pemphigoid, not pemphigus. Pemphigus vulgaris typically presents in middle age and commonly begins with oral involvement.

overallFeedback.feedback: Tense bullae + elderly patient + no oral lesions + negative Nikolsky = bullous pemphigoid (sub-epidermal, anti-BP180/BP230). Compare: pemphigus vulgaris has flaccid bullae, middle age, oral onset, positive Nikolsky (intra-epidermal, anti-desmoglein 3/1).
You correctly identified bullous pemphigoid — a sub-epidermal autoimmune blistering disease characterised by tense bullae, elderly onset, pruritus, and a negative Nikolsky's sign.
